core.title: Keep flow router declaration, runtime, route table and trace bilaterally bound
core.given: A consumer repository with a flow router declaration space (flow router route declarations among its plan artifacts) or a runtime route resolver
core.when: you add, change or delete any binding surface (flow router declaration, user/system flow artifact, runtime route resolution or user/system flow delegation, composition-root route table, trace emission or e2e trace test), or the detector reports a binding violation
core.then: Keep all five directions closed: every declared route resolves through the runtime route resolver to its declared userSystemFlowId (the user/system flow artifact exists); the route resolver resolves only declared routeIds/userSystemFlowIds before delegating user/system flow execution; every composition-root route-table mapping points at an existing declared flow router; every flow router with entrypoint.exposed=true is reachable through one of its entrypoint.actions wired into the route table; and every executed route emits trace metadata whose flowRouterId/routeId resolve to the declared route space.
prefer: Close the direction named in the violation: add the missing user/system flow artifact; remove or declare a hidden routeId/userSystemFlowId literal; repoint the route-table mapping at the real flow router declaration; wire the exposed flow router's entrypoint.action into the route table; assert only declared trace flowRouterId/routeId values.
If a flow router is genuinely internal, set entrypoint.exposed:false with a reason instead of wiring it.
Read core `entrypoint.exposed`/`entrypoint.actions` as owned by the core flow router schema; follow core if its name or shape changes.

Follow the additive call chain (core runtime spec): flow router declaration -> entrypoint.actions[] -> route-table action in the composition root -> the route resolver's resolve call -> its named resolution result (routeId, userSystemFlowId, category, guardId, resolutionStrategy, ...) -> user/system flow execution with the selected userSystemFlowId -> trace(flowRouterId, routeId, selectedUserSystemFlowId, ...), so the validator can resolve the trace back to the declared route.
avoid: Hidden routes: routeId/selectedUserSystemFlowId literals the route resolver resolves that are declared in no flow router declaration.
Parallel reachability fields (`entrypoints`, `runtime_exposure`, `station_actions`, `exposed_actions`, `reachability`) that fork core `entrypoint` — schema drift; replace them with core `entrypoint`.
Dangling route-table mappings, executed routes without trace emission, or trace assertions on undeclared values.
unless: Flow routers with entrypoint.exposed:false (internal-transition-only / library-only / planned-not-exposed) carry no route-table-reachability (declaration_to_route_table) obligation.
A tree with no flow router declaration space and no runtime route resolver is not a flow router system; the rule does not bite.
core.why: Bilateral binding is what makes flow router a route-control system rather than a description; any broken direction lets declaration, runtime, route table and trace drift apart silently, so it blocks CI.
evidence: The flow router binding check reports no violation for any of the five directions or schema drift on the consumer tree.
Each violation names its failing `direction` in evidence; the fix closes that direction.
verification: One repository-wide binding check walks the flow router declaration space, the user/system flow artifacts, the composition root's route table, the runtime route resolver and the e2e trace tests, reporting every violation under this single rule with the failing `direction` in evidence, plus a schema-drift signal when a parallel reachability field is used instead of the core `entrypoint`.
declaration_to_runtime: every declared route resolves through the route resolver to the declared userSystemFlowId — the route's user/system flow artifact must exist so the runtime can load it.

runtime_to_declaration: the route resolver never resolves a routeId/userSystemFlowId absent from the loaded declarations; a resolver returning a routeId/selectedUserSystemFlowId literal not declared in any flow router is a hidden route.

route_table_to_declaration: every composition-root flow router mapping ({flowRouterId, path}) points to an existing flow router declaration; a mapping whose path resolves to no file or names an undeclared flowRouterId is a dangling route.

declaration_to_route_table: every flow router with core entrypoint.exposed=true is reachable through one of its core entrypoint.actions wired into the route table to that flow router; the check consumes core entrypoint.exposed + entrypoint.actions and defines no parallel reachability field.

trace_to_declaration: every executed flow router route emits trace metadata resolving back to its declaration; a trace test asserting trace.routeId / trace.flowRouterId values absent from the declared route space does not bind the run to its declaration (core trace contract).

The enforced call model (core runtime spec, additive): flow router declaration -> entrypoint.actions[] -> route-table action in the composition root -> the route resolver's resolve call -> its named resolution result (routeId, userSystemFlowId, category, guardId, resolutionStrategy, ...) -> user/system flow execution with the selected userSystemFlowId -> trace(flowRouterId, routeId, selectedUserSystemFlowId, ...) -> the validator resolves the trace back to the declared route; each stack's resolver call, named resolution result and delegation call come from the profile's route-resolution idiom.

Ownership split: the core flow router schema owns the declaration schema and the shape/allowed values of `entrypoint`; this rule only READS those core fields to validate reachability against the route table and runtime traces in a consumer repo, and MUST NOT introduce `entrypoints`, `runtime_exposure`, `station_actions`, `exposed_actions`, `reachability` or any other parallel reachability field; if the core schema changes the field name or shape, the rule (and its checker and fixtures) follows core.
Term parallel_reachability_field: any non-core reachability field that forks the core `entrypoint` field; using one is schema drift.
Term hidden_route: a routeId/selectedUserSystemFlowId the route resolver resolves that is declared in no flow router declaration — a runtime-to-declaration binding break.

Term bilateral_binding: the property that flow router declaration, runtime resolution, route-table reachability and execution trace are bound in both directions so none can drift from the others undetected.
The check emits RAW facts only; the strict verdict is applied by a downstream gate.
Disposition strict, severity 1: a finding is not advisory — a broken binding direction blocks CI.

The check is proven by one fail fixture per direction (declaration_to_runtime, runtime_to_declaration, route_table_to_declaration, declaration_to_route_table, trace_to_declaration) and passes a clean tree.

values: flow router route/entrypoint declared, edited or removed
user/system flow artifact added, renamed or deleted
routeId/userSystemFlowId literal added in the runtime route resolver
route resolution or user/system flow delegation edited
trace emission added, edited or removed
route-table flow router mapping added, edited or removed
reachability field added to a flow router declaration

fires: A consumer repository has (or gains) a declared flow router route whose user/system flow artifact does not exist, e.g. a route added or a user/system flow artifact deleted/renamed.
The runtime route resolver returns a routeId/selectedUserSystemFlowId literal not declared in any flow router declaration.
A route-table flow router mapping points at a path with no declaration or an undeclared flowRouterId.
A flow router marked entrypoint.exposed=true has none of its entrypoint.actions wired in the route table.
An executed flow router route emits no trace metadata, or emits trace flowRouterId/routeId values that do not resolve to the declared route space.
An e2e trace test asserts a trace.routeId/flowRouterId absent from the declared route space.
A flow router declaration gains a field such as `reachability` or `station_actions` instead of core `entrypoint`.
The detector reports an existing binding violation in a tree the task did not otherwise touch on that surface.
A repo has a runtime route resolver but no flow router declaration space (or vice versa).
doesNotFire: A consumer tree with neither a flow router declaration space nor a runtime route resolver.
A flow router with entrypoint.exposed:false lacking a route-table action (only the declaration_to_route_table direction is exempt).
A flow router rendering owned by another stack's workspace package.

The runtime route-resolution call: the resolver that resolves a declared routeId to its user/system flow, the named resolution result it returns (routeId, userSystemFlowId, category, guardId, resolutionStrategy, ...), and the user/system flow delegation that executes the selected userSystemFlowId; every routeId/userSystemFlowId literal in the chain must be declared.

neutralityNotes: Renames: journey router / JOURNEY_MAP -> the composition root's route table (roles.composition_root.path + idiom.routing#route_table); FlowRouterRunner / FlowRunner -> the runtime route resolver and user/system flow delegation (roles.application.path + roles.runtime_components#route_resolver, extended this round to also bind the named resolution result FlowRouterResolution(routeId, userSystemFlowId, category, guardId, resolutionStrategy, ...)); flow router YAML -> flow router declaration; e2e/** -> the e2e_test role. Direction labels station_to_declaration / declaration_to_station became route_table_to_declaration / declaration_to_route_table; the Bun labels are preserved verbatim in bun.json (delivered as the reference example) and in the bunOnly finding-id entry. The bunOnly call chains (prefer[3], verifier_detail[6]) now quote the Bun rewrite verbatim, so the authoritative construct FlowRouterResolution is preserved exactly — no renamed or weakened variant. Core-design refs (afokapu/atdd#1246/#1248/#1249/#1251) are referenced narratively in the core ('core flow router schema', 'core runtime spec / trace contract') since the field names (entrypoint.exposed, entrypoint.actions, routeId, userSystemFlowId, flowRouterId, resolution fields, trace payload) are core-schema-owned and therefore stack-neutral; the numbered refs stay in the realization. Schema drift remains outside then (in prefer/avoid/verification) exactly as in Bun, and the strict disposition / severity 1 / RAW-facts-with-downstream-gate structure moved to core:verification per the notProfileKeys rule. activation.facts[1] (language) is only partly neutralizable: tooling.languages carries just the production-source language (typescript) per its vocabulary meaning; 'bun' is runtime/package-manager stack identity, not a language, so it stays bunOnly with the realization's scope sentence. Core activation facts carry no notes, so the facts[0] note ('presence of either the route space or a resolver makes the tree a flow router system') is carried by given, fires and doesNotFire. Three vocabulary keys are missing and proposed: layout.locations#flow_router_dir, idiom.routing#route_table, roles.runtime_components#route_resolver (documented scope and value extended this round to cover the named resolution result).
